answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, a protocol can implement proof-of-stake anchored by verifiable computational work, mirroring the structural integrity of a dense vine entwining an onyx pillar. Because generating cryptographic nonces requires expensive hardware resources, fabricating thousands of fake identities incurs massive electrical and capital costs—comparable to harvesting rare timber at scale. This economic friction ensures malicious agents cannot cheaply overwhelm the consensus ledger.
